meta.scope: Bolivia batch 3 — La Paz/El Alto metro, lithium (YLB / Salar de Uyuni), IDH and hydrocarbon royalties, major social programmes (Renta Dignidad, Juancito Pinto, Juana Azurduy), education/health presence, and trade-architecture notes (MERCOSUR accession, CAN).

candidates.title: La Paz / El Alto — dual-city metropolitan complex
candidates.description: Dual-city capital complex: La Paz (seat of government) and the adjacent, rapidly grown city of El Alto on the Altiplano. Primary urban domain for labour, income, poverty and social-programme analysis in the western highlands.
candidates.notes: Lived-economy core of the western highlands. El Alto in particular is a dense, commercially dynamic, largely Aymara city that grew from migration; multidimensional poverty readings remain elevated. Continuously cited as a distinct geographic domain in household-survey and urban-poverty analysis.

candidates.title: Yacimientos de Litio Bolivianos (YLB) — state lithium company
candidates.publisher: YLB / Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energía
candidates.description: State company charged with the industrialisation of Bolivia’s lithium resources, centred on the Salar de Uyuni (world’s largest known resources). Contracts with Chinese and Russian partners for direct-extraction plants.
candidates.notes: Strategic future-resource node. Production remains far below commercial scale relative to Chile and Argentina; recent contracts (CBC/China, Uranium One/Russia) aim to scale direct lithium extraction. Continuously cited in industrial-policy and fiscal-revenue outlook analysis.

candidates.title: Salar de Uyuni — lithium resource base
candidates.description: World’s largest known lithium resource (salt flat in Potosí department). Geographic and symbolic core of Bolivia’s lithium strategy.
candidates.notes: Foundational natural-resource node. Continuously cited as the physical base of the lithium industrialisation effort; also a national and Indigenous heritage symbol.

candidates.title: Impuesto Directo a los Hidrocarburos (IDH)
candidates.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas Públicas / YPFB
candidates.description: Direct tax on hydrocarbons. Historically the central fiscal instrument that channelled gas rents into national and subnational budgets and social programmes.
candidates.notes: Structural fiscal node of the gas era. As gas production and exports decline, IDH revenues have fallen sharply, tightening the fiscal space that once financed large social transfers and public investment.

candidates.title: Renta Dignidad — universal old-age pension
candidates.description: Non-contributory universal pension for older adults. Flagship social-protection programme financed in part from hydrocarbon rents.
candidates.notes: Lived-economy social node. Continuously cited in poverty-reduction and inequality analysis; one of the most visible redistributive instruments of the post-2006 period.

candidates.title: Bono Juancito Pinto — school attendance cash transfer
candidates.description: Conditional cash transfer paid to schoolchildren (and families) to encourage enrolment, attendance and completion. Covers primary and secondary levels.
candidates.notes: Core education–social linkage. Continuously cited in education-access and poverty-reduction analysis; complements administrative enrolment statistics.

candidates.title: Bono Juana Azurduy — maternal and early-childhood transfer
candidates.description: Conditional cash transfer for pregnant women and children under two, aimed at improving maternal and child health outcomes.
candidates.notes: Core health–social linkage. Continuously cited in maternal/child-health and poverty-reduction analysis.

candidates.title: Sistema educativo — cobertura y gasto
candidates.description: Education-system statistics (enrolment, attendance, institutional counts) and public education expenditure. Complements the Juancito Pinto transfer.
candidates.notes: Education remains a major functional allocation and a visible social priority. Attendance and completion gaps persist, especially in rural and highland areas.

candidates.title: Sistema de salud — cobertura y gasto
candidates.description: Public health-system statistics and health expenditure. Complements the Juana Azurduy transfer and the broader social-protection architecture.
candidates.notes: Health access and out-of-pocket spending remain structural concerns, especially outside the main urban centres. Continuously tracked in social and fiscal analysis.

candidates.title: MERCOSUR accession & Andean Community (CAN) membership
candidates.description: Bolivia’s dual regional-integration status: full member of the Andean Community and (more recently) member of MERCOSUR. Shapes preferential trade access and external-agenda positioning.
referenced_by: Discussion of Bolivia’s participation in the MERCOSUR–EU agreement
candidates.notes: Core trade-architecture node. Bolivia’s MERCOSUR membership is recent; full participation in the MERCOSUR–EU preferential arrangement is still being clarified. CAN remains the older Andean preferential framework.

proposed_edges.basis: La Paz and El Alto are primary geographic domains of the household survey.
YLB’s industrialisation effort is centred on the Salar de Uyuni resource base.
IDH revenues are directly tied to hydrocarbon production and prices.
Hydrocarbon rents (including IDH) have been a primary financing source for the universal pension.
The cash transfer is designed to support enrolment and attendance within the formal education system.
The maternal/child transfer is designed to improve utilisation of health services.
Preferential access under CAN and MERCOSUR structures a large share of regional trade.
